newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, stable trend to last.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, stable trend to last.

text.p: Croatian stocks rebounded on Friday, closing the week mostly higher in a much more buoyant trade, and the stable trend, with no spectacular price movements in the near future, was likely to last.
"Investors' confidence has returned, though now they are much more cautious than before," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage.
He referred to a recent government announcement to annul some 9,000 employee buyout contracts, which scared away foreign buyers. The threat was later withdrawn.

"Nothing dramatic should happen in the coming days," he said, predicting that most trading would be made with the fully-listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, with food processor Podravka and confectioner Kras to follow.
Volume was doubled at 21,718 shares, and turnover at 20 million kuna accounted for more than a half of this week's trading with total weekly turnover at 35.8 million kuna.
Of fourteen active issues, eight were up, three down, two flat and one was traded for the first time.
Top gainer on volume of only 107 shares was shipper Atlantska Plovidba, up 100 kuna to 180 from early September.
Most active Zagrebacka Banka which added five kuna to 1,000, sold 17,119 shares. price. Its global depository receipts (GDRs) traded slightly higher at $19.81 on Seaq International.
Pliva closed 100 kuna up at 13,600, trading 153 shares. Its GDRs fetched $51.625 in London.

The bank's E-series was the biggest of the three decliners, falling 20 kuna to close at 430, with 33 units sold. Hotelier Istraturist edged down 10 kuna to 210, selling only 22 shares, while Kras lost five kuna to 520 with 125 units sold.

Traders speculate that Podravka, which gained seven kuna to close at 233 on volume of 2,4354 shares, could soon become the 'hot stock' on the market. But Zelimorski said it would not rise much above 230 kuna.
Among gainers were also hoteliers Jadranturist, closing two kuna higher at 290, and Riviera Porec, up five kuna to 150, selling 196 and 500 units, respectively.
Hotelier Suncani Hvar was flat at 60 and 1,600 kuna, while another hotel stock Imperial Rab traded for the first time at 200 kuna, selling 52 shares. ( 5.3719 kuna = $1.)
